bounds.scope: Residual scripts/ classes: Python SDK/SSH executable builds, client catalog and route gates, plugin metadata, persistence/catalog/snapshot helpers, release plumbing and co-located tests.

mechanisms.title: Replay spill locators are stable logical names scoped to one saved run
mechanisms.problem: A snapshot replay records logical spill locators so a later replay can refer to the same tool result. If two concurrent replays of the same session/call allocate the same physical file, one overwrites the other's bytes; if a locator saved by one run maps into another run, replay reads unrelated content. Keeping locator text stable while routing it to a run-private physical file is the hard part.
triggers: recording or replaying a snapshot that spills a large tool result
running two snapshot sessions concurrently, including out-of-order allocation
changing the spill store, filesystem adapter or locator root
disposing or restoring a replay fork
obligations: Concurrent replays with identical owner, source, suggested name and content must produce equal-length logical locators, but distinct physical files inside each run's own root. Allocation completion order must not matter.

The logical locator must start with the recorded locatorRoot. The spec asserts ref.bytes equals the saved content's UTF-8 byte length and that concurrent locators have equal string length; it does not assert that locator text length equals the recorded byte count. Reading through fs.resolve must return exactly the saved content.

Only locators saved by the current run may resolve or map to a host path. A descendant of locatorRoot (locatorRoot + separator) that is not mapped throws 'not saved by this run' from both resolve and processPathFromHostPath; the bare locatorRoot without a trailing separator passes through as an ordinary path. Ordinary paths outside the root pass through unchanged.
The implementation rejects a spill backend locator outside the run's live root before mapping it; this guarantee is not in the spec's direct assertions.

Disposing the locator plugin must remove the mapping. After disposal, resolving the old locator must not stat the old physical file and processPathFromHostPath must treat the locator as an ordinary passthrough value, so stale locators cannot read a previous run's data.
The test must cover both allocation orders because Promise.all preserves input order, not completion order, and concurrent creation is the failure mode.
steps: Allocate a per-run physical root and register a logical-to-physical mapping when a spill is saved.
Keep the logical locator text stable and equal-length; use a hidden per-run suffix or table rather than embedding the physical path.
Resolve and reverse-map only through the saved-run table; throw 'not saved by this run' otherwise.
Pass ordinary host paths through untouched.
Dispose the mapping with the replay fork and assert the old locator no longer reaches the old file.

enforcement.implementation: scripts/snapshot-spill-locators.ts implements the run-private mapping and backend-locator containment; scripts/snapshot-spill-locators.spec.ts drives it with LocalSpillStore, LocalFileSystem and the replay locator plugin
enforcement.trust: Locator prefix, content byte count (ref.bytes), equal-length concurrent locators, physical privacy, saved-run resolution, passthrough and post-dispose behavior are asserted against real temp roots; backend containment and bare-root passthrough are implementation-reading guarantees. Cross-process collision is not exercised
enforcement.failure: A shared physical path silently returns another run's bytes; an unsaved locator maps to an arbitrary file; disposal leaves a stale mapping that reads deleted or unrelated data
exceptions: ordinary absolute paths are intentionally pass-through
the locator root may be a synthetic POSIX path on Windows

mechanisms.applicability: Replay/snapshot harnesses that virtualize spill files and can run sessions concurrently. Backend-specific details are parameterized; the saved-run scoping rule is generic.

migration.implementation: Keep logical-locator stability and run-private physical allocation. Replace LocalSpillStore/LocalFileSystem with the target harness adapters and keep the same assertions.

positive.scenario: two concurrent runs save the same content
positive.check: equal-length locators, distinct physical paths, both contents readable

rejection.scenario: resolve an unsaved locator under the locator root
rejection.check: throws 'not saved by this run' from resolve and reverse mapping

recovery.scenario: dispose the locator plugin after saving
recovery.check: old locator no longer maps to the old physical file; stat is undefined

mechanisms.limitations: The spec covers one in-process spill store and filesystem adapter. The locator text length is only compared between concurrent runs; it is not asserted to equal the content byte count. The bare locatorRoot passes through, and backend containment is implementation-only. It does not prove cross-process collision behavior, crash recovery, or that every locator-independent code path uses the mapping. The synthetic locatorRoot may not reproduce every Windows path-shape edge.

mechanisms.title: Python runtime wheels: remove only distribution test trees and rewrite RECORD safely
mechanisms.problem: The unpacked Python runtime ships NumPy and pandas wheels. Their test suites dominate the extracted payload, but deleting too much removes testing helpers, compiled extension support modules, licenses or data needed at runtime; rewriting RECORD naively drops quoted comma paths or hashes, and a malformed record can cause deletion before the tool notices the file is corrupt.
triggers: changing the bundled NumPy or pandas version
changing the primary-runtime wheel unpack/prune step
adding a distribution whose test directory layout differs
RECORD parsing or CSV handling changes
obligations: Remove every directory named tests anywhere under the numpy and pandas distribution trees, including nested and empty ones. Keep testing helper modules and files such as numpy/testing/__init__.py, pandas/testing.py, pandas/_testing, compiled *_multiarray_tests binaries, data files and dist-info licenses; do not remove similarly named tests under other distributions (other/tests, numpy_extra/tests).

RECORD is CSV with a sha256 digest and size per row. Rewrite it with the original hashes and sizes, keep the self-row and exactly the retained rows. The spec's row helper writes every path quoted with a base64url sha256; assertions expect unquoted non-comma paths and quoted comma paths. Embedded-quote, escape and CRLF forms are not exercised.

Validate every RECORD before deleting anything for that distribution. Unterminated quotes, empty rows, missing hash/size rows and empty files must abort with 'invalid wheel RECORD' while test files remain intact.
The second pruning run must be a no-op (byte-identical RECORD), and the source .whl archive must never be modified; pruning is applied to the unpacked site-packages tree only.
Tests read the lock-pinned NumPy/pandas versions; the spec does not execute a version-mismatch negative case, so mismatch behavior is not proven.
steps: Read and validate each target distribution's RECORD before deleting anything.
Delete only the target tests directory trees.
Rewrite RECORD with retained rows and original hashes/sizes, preserving CSV quoting.
Leave the archive untouched; assert a second run changes nothing.

enforcement.implementation: scripts/primary-runtime/prune-python-tests.ts (prunePrimaryRuntimePythonTests, Papa.parse/unparse) and scripts/primary-runtime/prepare.ts (unpackPrimaryRuntimeWheel); scripts/primary-runtime/prune-python-tests.spec.ts drives them on a real zip
enforcement.trust: File selection, RECORD round-trip for the constructed rows, archive immutability, idempotence and malformed-record refusal are asserted on a real zip built per test. Exotic CSV quoting, omitted RECORD rows, and version-mismatch behavior are not executed
enforcement.failure: Pruning removes a runtime helper or license, RECORD disagrees with extracted files, a comma path corrupts the CSV, or a malformed record leads to deleting tests without a valid inventory
exceptions: test directories of distributions other than NumPy/pandas are untouched by design
the wheel archive keeps its original contents; only the extracted tree is pruned

mechanisms.applicability: Packaging pipelines that bundle Python wheels into a single executable or runtime and need to cut test payload without breaking wheel metadata. Distribution names and test-directory conventions are parameterizable. The wheel/platform policy itself is owned by supply-chain-python-runtime; this mechanism owns only pruning and RECORD integrity.

migration.implementation: Keep validate-before-delete and RECORD rewrite semantics. Parameterize the distribution names, version lock and test-directory layout; keep the malformed-record rejection and the archive-untouched assertion.
requiredSupport: lock file with pinned distribution versions

positive.scenario: prune NumPy/pandas tests from an unpacked wheel
positive.check: removed trees gone; retained files byte-identical; RECORD has retained rows plus self-row

rejection.scenario: malformed RECORD rows or empty RECORD
rejection.check: throws 'invalid wheel RECORD' and leaves test files intact

recovery.check: second run leaves RECORD byte-identical; archive unchanged

mechanisms.limitations: Only NumPy/pandas are covered. The RECORD validator is exercised on synthetic rows; the spec's row helper writes every path quoted with a base64url sha256 and the assertions expect unquoted non-comma paths, so embedded-quote/escape/CRLF forms or a wheel whose RECORD omits rows may behave differently. No version-mismatch negative case is executed. Pruned RECORD intentionally differs from the archive's original RECORD, so archive-level verification must not be used to validate the extracted tree.

mechanisms.title: Client slot catalog: teach every registrable slot within a bounded per-slot report
mechanisms.problem: A model asked to add UI to a dynamic package must know which slots exist, which register options each kind accepts, what props the component receives, who already occupies the seat and when the seat exists. That contract is spread across SlotMap merges and register call sites. Dumping the whole client type graph into a catalog makes one slot answer more expensive than reading the source, while an undocumented or unresolvable slot silently produces an unusable catalog entry.
triggers: declaring or changing a SlotMap slot
changing register/registerFactory options or a slot kind/scope
changing owner props, standard props or inject context
adding a registrant that occupies or shadows shipped UI
regenerating or reviewing the model-facing client catalog
obligations: SlotMap merges are the authority. Every catalog key must be declared exactly once across merges; duplicates are a contract violation because the merge is silent. kind must be a literal single/list/keyed/chain and scope a literal root/session/session-maybe. Duplicate detection is asserted on synthetic inputs; the real-workspace test asserts entry count/fields, not key uniqueness.

Every slot must carry registrant-side JSDoc prose (what to pass, what the component receives, whom a registration replaces, what absence looks like). An owner prop type must resolve to an exported declaration; otherwise the catalog cannot teach what the component receives.

Every registration must target a declared slot or be a factory; every declared child slot must be typed by some SlotMap merge. A registration into an undeclared slot is dead or the scan has a blind spot.

Owner props expand only the named owner type plus its top-level composed aliases; field value types stay references so one slot does not expand the Session graph. Declarations longer than 1200 characters are truncated with an explicit marker, never silently cut; truncation and ambiguous exported-type dropping are implementation-only, with no direct test.

One slot's expanded report (doc, example, owner props, register-option docs, standard props, owner-prop references, occupants) must stay within 122 lines. Over-budget slots fail the generator; fix by narrowing the owner share or tightening prose, never by raising the budget. The 122-line and 1200-character numbers are source calibrations.

Register options are curated per cardinality (single none; list id/order/label; keyed key; chain select). Do not teach priority: the browser facade assigns one lower than every shipped entry. Teach inject/remount semantics and the no-import/CSS-theme constraints in the shared notes.

The generator emits a data module consumed by the host toolset and must not import a client runtime module. Scan all matching .ts/.tsx sources rather than a reachable-export closure; drop ambiguous exported type names; parse .tsx as TSX; restrict registration receivers to slots or *.slots and names to string literals. The last three behaviors are implementation-only.

Intentional repetition across seats (register options, framework props) is marked for clone detection with jscpd annotations rather than a config exception. The generated file starts with ignore markers and closes them.
The normal CLI writes the artifact; --check must fail for stale or missing output and must never write. Regeneration is the only remedy.
steps: Declare the SlotMap member with literal kind/scope and registrant-facing JSDoc.
Export any owner props interface the slot hands to registrants.
Register with slots.inject and a literal slot name; name child slots only when they exist while the entry is mounted.
Run the generator and fix all contract violations; run --check to confirm the committed catalog is fresh.
Review the per-slot report size and trim owner shares/prose before considering any budget change.

enforcement.implementation: scripts/gen-client-catalog.ts + scripts/slot-walk.ts; scripts/gen-client-catalog.spec.ts pins contract validation on hand-built inputs, the 122-line budget and the real-workspace entry/field surface. The spec does not execute --check, the 1200-character truncation or ambiguous-type dropping; those remain implementation-only or a separate CLI step
enforcement.trust: Kind/scope liveness, duplicate keys and declaration resolution are mechanically checked on synthetic fixtures; the 122-line budget and the real-workspace >30 entry/field surface are also exercised. --check freshness was not executed in this slice; 1200-character truncation, ambiguous exported-type dropping and real-workspace key uniqueness are implementation-only. Whether the prose actually teaches a registrant, and whether the rendered report has the claimed token cost, require review
enforcement.failure: A model receives a catalog entry it cannot register (missing declaration, wrong options, undeclared target), or one slot's answer consumes the context needed to implement it; a stale committed artifact diverges from the source contract
exceptions: factory-registered slots need no ordinary declaration
slots declared by the runtime itself are described as built-in
ambiguous exported type names are omitted rather than guessed

mechanisms.applicability: Host tool catalogs that project a compile-time registry into model-facing context, especially browser slot systems. The 122-line and 1200-character numbers are source-repo calibrations and must be re-derived for another model/context budget.

migration.implementation: Keep SlotMap-as-authority, fail-closed validation, one-level owner expansion and the report budget. Parameterize the slots module name, source globs, kind/scope sets, register-option table and the 122/1200 budgets; keep --check non-writing.
requiredSupport: TypeScript compiler API or equivalent AST parser

positive.scenario: a documented literal slot with resolvable owner props and a declared registration
positive.check: collectSlotEntries returns an entry; generated catalog matches --check
positive.note: Spec covers judgement and the 122-line budget; --check freshness is a separate CLI step and was not executed here.

rejection.scenario: duplicate key, non-literal kind/scope, missing JSDoc, unresolvable owner type, registration into an undeclared slot, child key not typed
rejection.check: each becomes a reported contract violation

recovery.check: generator fails; narrow the owner share or prose and rerun; no budget raise

mechanisms.limitations: Report line count is a proxy for rendered context cost, not a measured token count. The scan is lexical and does not resolve conditional/mapped types; one-level owner expansion can still omit a cross-package shape. The real-workspace test asserts >30 entries and fields, not key uniqueness; 1200-character truncation and ambiguous exported-type dropping have no direct test. The 122-line and 1200-character numbers are source calibrations, not portable targets. --check freshness is a separate CLI step and was not executed in this slice. Specs assert generator judgement, not the host tool's rendered answer.

mechanisms.title: Windows-safe script plumbing: JS entrypoints, tar cwd and junction-first cleanup
mechanisms.problem: Release and fixture scripts written on POSIX fail or destroy state on Windows: spawnSync cannot start a .cmd shim, GNU tar interprets the colon in C:/... as a remote host, and recursive deletion follows junctions into the repository's real scripts/node_modules/tsx directories. These failures are platform-specific and can be irreversible.
triggers: calling pnpm or another package-manager shim from Node
reading a tarball by absolute Windows path
cleaning a fixture tree that contains junctions
adding a Windows CI lane or moving release helpers
obligations: Resolve pnpm to a JavaScript-launchable command: either pnpm itself or a node executable whose first argument names pnpm. Do not depend on pnpm.cmd or a shell. The command must actually run (--version) on the host, not just be assembled.
When GNU tar reads an archive, set cwd to the archive's directory and pass its basename. Never pass an absolute Windows path containing a drive colon; tar would treat it as a remote host.

Before recursively deleting a fixture tree, walk it and unlink every junction/symlink. Only then remove the directory. On POSIX the walk is effectively a no-op because unlink/rm do not follow symlinks. Never call rmSync or git worktree remove on a tree that still contains junctions.

Windows removal must be bounded: rmSync with maxRetries 50 and retryDelay 200ms (10-second window) to absorb asynchronous handle release. Do not retry unboundedly; do not swallow non-EPERM errors; a bounded window must not pin afterEach cleanup.

The process and tarball helpers must be tested with real processes and real archives: list members and read packed identity beside the archive, and assert pnpm reports a version. Mocks alone do not prove Windows launchability.

The junction-first cleanup helper is implementation-only in this slice: release/process.spec.ts does not call removeFixtureSafely or unlinkFixtureLinks, and no cited test creates a junction and proves deletion order. Callers must use the helper; the helper cannot force that.
steps: Resolve pnpm to a JS entrypoint and spawn it without a shell.
For tar, chdir to the archive directory and use the basename.
For fixture teardown, call the helper that unlinks links first, then removes with the bounded retry.
Add real-process tests on a Windows runner; do not substitute command-shape assertions for the real probe.

enforcement.implementation: scripts/release/process.spec.ts plus scripts/test-fixture-cleanup.ts (unlinkFixtureLinks/removeFixtureSafely); the release process/tarball helpers under test are separate owner modules
enforcement.trust: Command shape, real pnpm --version, real tar member/identity reads and the cleanup order are mechanically checkable; the destructive junction behavior and handle-release timing depend on a real Windows runner
enforcement.failure: pnpm cannot start, tar reads a drive letter as a host and fails/targets the wrong machine, or fixture cleanup deletes the repository's own scripts/node_modules; alternatively afterEach flakes on EPERM
exceptions: POSIX removes symlinks without following them, so the unlink walk is a no-op there
a fixture tree known to contain no junctions may skip the explicit walk, but the shared helper should still be used

mechanisms.applicability: Cross-platform release/fixture scripts that must run on Windows CI. PNPM_HOME/env resolution and retry counts are environment-specific; the no-shell, no-drive-colon and link-first rules are generic. Link-first deletion specializes engineering-untrusted-subprocess; this mechanism adds the pnpm JS entrypoint, tar cwd and bounded Windows retry.

migration.implementation: Keep the JS-entrypoint pnpm launch, tar cwd/basename rule, link-first cleanup and bounded retry. Reuse the helper rather than reimplementing rmSync in each suite.

positive.scenario: pnpm --version via the resolved JS entry; tar lists members beside the archive
positive.check: version matches and members/identity are returned

rejection.scenario: absolute Windows archive path passed to tar
rejection.note: The spec comment documents the failure; it does not itself invoke the bad path.

recovery.scenario: fixture deletion hits a junction or EPERM
recovery.check: unlink links first; bounded retries drain handles; real target directories survive

mechanisms.limitations: The specs prove command shape and real tar/pnpm behavior on the current platform; the destructive junction traversal is not reproduced end to end here, and no cited test creates a junction or asserts the retry window/non-EPERM pass-through. The 50x200ms retry window is tuned to the source repository's runner load and should be re-measured.
